records.title: California Residential Private Permitting Review Act: residential building permits.
records.description: Known as the California Residential Private Permitting Review Act , this bill requires counties prepare and post a fee schedule online. Local building depts must provide applicants with estimated timeframes for plan checks. If a dept needs more than 30 days to complete a plan check, applicants can hire private professionals to perform it. These private professionals must submit an affidavit and report to the building department, which then has 14 days to issue the permit or to notify applicants of non-compliance. The bill applies to specific new constructions and modifications of residential buildings.

records.title: Adaptive reuse: streamlining: incentives.
records.description: Would allow local govts to ministerially approve adaptive reuse projects if in urbanized areas, satisfy affordability criteria, and preserve historic resources where applicable. Rental projects must include either 8% very low income and 5% extremely low income units, or 15% lower income units.  Owner-occupied projects must offer either 30% of units at moderate-income affordability or 15% at lower-income affordability. Local gov't can establish investment incentive programs to support these projects.

records.title: Low-impact camping areas.
records.description: The Special Occupancy Parks Act currently governs the construction, maintenance, and use of special occupancy parks, which include recreational vehicle parks and campgrounds. This bill specifies that "low-impact camping areas" are excluded from this definition if located in counties with specific ordinances for such camping. The bill outlines conditions for private property owners offering low-impact camping sites and hosting platforms, requiring these areas to comply with local waste disposal and noise regulations. Additionally, counties that permit low-impact camping must create a registry of these sites and inform HCD of their decision. Low-impact camping areas are defined as private properties rented for temporary recreational stays that do not qualify as commercial lodging facilities.

records.title: California Factory-Built Housing Law.
records.description: Updates the California Factory-Built Housing Law's scope to include factory-built developments, which are defined as projects using factory-built housing for at least 50% of residential square footage. Shifts inspection and enforcement responsibilities entirely to HCD, removing local government's previous role. Requires plan approvals to be done by unit serial number. Would allow approved plans to be used in subsequent development projects within the same or subsequent building code cycles, with the HCD limiting its review to only new or unapproved portions of plans. Maintains local jurisdictions' authority to regulate zoning, setbacks, and aesthetic requirements.

records.title: Surface mining: Metropolitan Water District of Southern California.
records.description: The SMARA allows the Metropolitan Water District of Southern California (MWD) to create a master reclamation plan for mining operations within certain counties.  The current provisions that allow MWD to prepare this master reclamation plan are set to expire on January 1, 2026. This bill proposes to extend provisions until January 1, 2041 and would require local govt acting as lead agencies to continue their review duties, creating a state-mandated local program.

records.title: Local ordinances: administrative fines or penalties.
records.description: (FYI) Existing law allows local agencies to impose administrative fines or penalties for ordinance violations. The proposed bill would enhance enforcement by allowing agencies to file a certified copy of a final order directing payment of fines with a superior court clerk, who must then enter judgment according to the order. The bill also  permits local agencies to create a system to collect fines by placing a lien on the land where the violation occurred, if a specific notice is served.

records.title: Climate change: short-lived climate pollutants: organic waste reduction.
records.description: Would authorize a local govt to include organic material used as a beneficial agricultural amendment towards its recovered organic waste procurement target if the material is processed at a facility using specified approved technologies, and if the material is licensed for end use as an agricultural fertilizer by the FDA and the material is not derived from, or processed using, specified activities relating to the final deposition or management of solid waste.

records.title: Community colleges: housing: local zoning regulations: exemption.
records.description: allows California community college districts to bypass local zoning ordinances for university housing projects on their own property, provided certain conditions are met. If these projects include housing for faculty and staff, the bill mandates that some units be offered at affordable rents to those with extremely low and lower incomes. The bill asserts that its provisions address issues of statewide interest, affecting all cities, including charter cities.

records.title: Planning and zoning: housing element: regional housing needs allocation.
records.description: (FYI) Requires HCD develop a standardized reporting format for actions taken to further fair housing by December 31, 2026. For HE revisions, the timeline for determining housing needs and consulting with councils of governments is extended from 2 years to 3 years, and from 26 months to 38 months, respectively. Counties forming subregional entities for housing distribution now have up to 34 months before revisions, while the council of governments has up to 31 months to determine housing need distribution among subregions.

records.title: Planning and Zoning Law: postentitlement phase permits: Housing Accountability Act.
records.description: Would limit local agencies to 2 plan checks, allow agencies to deny applications not compliant with permit standards after 2 reviews, and reduce the time frame for review--Smaller housing projects (25 units or fewer), have 30 business days; for larger projects (26 units or more), 60 business days for review completion. Reduces appeal timeline to 30 business days for smaller projects and 45 business days for larger projects. If a federal or state agency requires review of a permit application, the local agency's review time will be paused (tolled) until that review is complete, with the local agency required to notify the applicant within 3 business days of the tolling and resumption of the time limit.

If passed, APR can include number of units in an existing multifamily building that were converted to affordable housing via long-term affordability covenants/restrictions that require the unit to be available to persons or families of varying low income at an affordable rent or affordable housing cost for at least 55 years, if the units meet certain criteria.
